title.narrative: Emergency and Recovery Responses to conflict affected communities in Yambio Western Equatoria.

description.narrative: On the 5th of February 2025, according to the Rapid Needs Assessment developed as part of a START alert, armed youths from Pibor Administrative Area attacked cattle camps in Ayii and Nyolo. The office of the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) reported that overall, 42,369 people were displaced due to the escalating conflict in Magwi County, Eastern Equatoria State. In Yambio, Food insecurity is being driven by conflict and insecurity (especially in Yambio and Zara Counties), dry spells, weeds and crop pest infestations, and inadequate access to agricultural tools that have negatively impacted on crop production and the first season harvest. CTP proposes a livelihoods-based emergency project in response to the ongoing conflict and its associated impacts in 2 counties because of its geography and climate. The proposed action aims at saving lives, addressing the immediate and medium-term needs and improving access to improved agricultures services, therefore, improving the food and nutrition security of the conflict affected communities and increasing their resilience to famine and disaster risks and shocks. The project targets primarily conflict affected IDPs and host Communities and returnees. In response to the ongoing food insecurity crisis, CTP proposes a livelihood-based emergency and recovery project in response to the ongoing conflict and its associated impacts in the two Counties (Magwi and Yambio) of South Sudan. The proposed action aims at saving lives, addressing the immediate and medium-term needs and improving access to improved agricultures and livestock services, enhance the skills and knowledge of small holder farmers for quality agricultural produce for market and increase household income therefore improving the food and nutrition security of the conflict affected communities and increasing their resilience to famine and disaster risks and shocks.
